title: What's the meaning of the ending shot of The Spider's Stratagem (1970) ?

commenti.body:
My personal interpretation is that it shows Athos is now caught in the spider's web/strategem since he became just like the town conspirators.

Throught the whole film Athos is trying to discover the truth about his father, but the entire town seems to be lying or being evasive to him, they all worship the comfortable myth that his father was a revolutionary hero because they need it.

When Athos discovers the truth and yet still refuses to say it, still plays along with the lie, he becomes part of it, part of the town.

That's a good interpretation, it really opened up a new perspective on the film for me. But the question still lingers as to why the train tracks were shown at the end covered with grass, that's what perplexes me so much

Bertolucci likes to finish his films on an enigmatic note. One striking final image to stick with you. Maybe the Grass growing out of the concrete is symbolism for how the truth of his father's death is now revealed. Although for me, the train delayed is the main symbol for the final scene. It starts at the station and it ends at the station. But the train is not here yet, perhaps a part of him would never truly escape that town. In other words, I agree with the second interpretation that you offered
I like your reading here. Bertolucci's protagonists are cowards in one way or another, so I think you're right on the money with what was intended

I think the other comment about Athos being caught inside or even complicit in the strategem is on point.  

The Borges story (The Theme of the Traitor and the Hero) on which the movie is based ends like this:

> Ryan realized that he, too, was part of Nolan's plot...  After long and stubborn deliberation, he decided to silence the discovery.  He published a book dedicated to the hero's glory; that too, perhaps, had been foreseen.

With that in mind, I felt like the effect of zooming out and drawing a bit of attention to the camera's motion, on top of the slightly unnerving and unexpected view of undisturbed grass (maybe suggesting the train was never going to come and never will, even the tracks are part of the show or artifice the town creates) was kind of pointing us toward the movie itself being part of the myth-making.  

Or maybe that's me bringing the short story into the meaning of the film more than it should be, idk.

Speaking of obscure adaptions of Borges stories, any chance you know how to find The Sidewalks of Saturn?  Never been able to find it online even though the fantastic Invasión, which it is a loose sequel to, is free on youtube.

Personally I see it as a touch of surrealism, a visual metaphor for how trapped people can become in a web of deceit, of our myths.

Because yeah it's the same train station he used to get there in the first place, and he clearly didn't spend much time in the town.
I have seen a version of it online, but without subtitles. Are you fine with it or do you need them?
Ahh that's a shame, I could stumble through but would be pausing it constantly
Ok it's on the internet archive and youtube under it's original title, but yeah obviously super annoying in that case
Now that you mention it, this gives reason to my second interpretation about Athos being trapped in the town as well. Thanks for replying!
It's just like in The Conformist, with Trintignant staring back at the camera. I see what you mean by that final, enigmatic image.
You could download the subtitles from [here](https://www.opensubtitles.com/en/subtitles/las-veredas-de-saturno-720pthefoolishwatcher-mkv) and use them with the video file
